notes: Joomla has no default account lockout by default, so a wordlist attack on /administrator is viable. Target admin first; the http_default_pass list catches most lab setups.

recommended.note: Use the cracked admin login to plant a template webshell.
Auth'd directory traversal as an alternative post-login path.

name: Joomla - Admin Brute Force
description: Brute-forces the Joomla administrator login. Recovered admin access allows code execution via the template editor.

defense.why_it_works: Joomla's /administrator/index.php login form does not rate-limit or lock accounts by default. joomla-brute.py submits credential pairs, checking for successful authentication redirect.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to /administrator/. No CAPTCHA or lockout policy. Valid wordlist matching default credentials.
defense.impact: Admin access grants template editing (webshell), extension installation, and complete site control.
defense.detection: High-volume POST requests to /administrator/index.php from one IP. PHP session creation spikes. WAF alert on login endpoint rate-limit.
defense.artifacts: Joomla error log (failed auth events) | Web server access log (POST /administrator/index.php at high rate)
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web sourcetype=access_combined uri_path="/administrator/index.php" status=401 OR status=403 OR (method=POST status=200)
| stats count by clientip, bin(_time, 1m)
| where count>20
defense.elastic_kql: event.category:web AND url.path:"/administrator/index.php" AND (http.response.status_code:(401 OR 403) OR http.request.method:POST)
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem =~ "/administrator/index.php"
| summarize attempts=count(), fails=countif(scStatus in (401,403)) by cIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where attempts > 20
| sort by attempts desc
// Joomla admin login brute force
defense.sigma_rules: web_login_bruteforce (high-rate POST to /administrator/index.php from one IP)
defense.prevention: Enforce account lockout via Joomla Admin Tools plugin. Require 2FA for all admin accounts. Move or rename the admin URL. Block /administrator/ from public IPs.
defense.misconfiguration: Joomla administrator login at /administrator/ publicly reachable with no lockout, no 2FA, and a weak default password.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Joomla default
# No lockout policy
# /administrator/ accessible from 0.0.0.0
defense.secure_config:
# Admin Tools plugin: lockout after 5 failures
# Joomla Global Config: Two Factor Authentication required
# Apache
<Directory /var/www/html/administrator>
  Require ip 10.0.0.0/8
</Directory>
defense.evasion: Obfuscate the injected template webshell and remove it after; blend admin actions into normal usage; avoid leaving the malicious extension/template enabled.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review IIS Web Server logs, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Brute-forces the Joomla administrator login:
  python3 joomla-brute.py  the brute tool
  -u http://<url>          the Joomla site
  -w <wordlist>            the password list
  -usr <user>              the admin username to attack
Recovered admin access allows code execution via the template editor.
